findings.state_artifact: tests-e2e/account-shots/name-whitespace-only.png (adversarial repro, not in original GStack quartet)
findings.evidence:
account-v2.jsx:467 `

Content de
te revoir,
{knownFirstDisplay || 'chef'} !

` — knownFirstDisplay derives from `lcReadKnownFirst()`, which is `localStorage.getItem(LC_KNOWN_FIRST_KEY) || null`. If lc_known_first is a whitespace-only string (e.g. ' '), it is truthy in JS, so the `|| 'chef'` fallback never triggers. Reproduced by seeding lc_known_first=' ' directly and loading state (c): heading renders 'CONTENT DE / TE REVOIR, / !' — a bare orange exclamation mark with a visible gap where the name should be. Screenshot captured independently (not part of the original 26/26 run, which only ever exercises FIRST='Julie').
findings.fix_hint: account-v2.jsx:449 — change `lcReadKnownFirst() || form.first || ''` to trim before the truthiness check, e.g. `(lcReadKnownFirst() || form.first || '').trim()`, so downstream `|| 'chef'` catches whitespace-only values too. NOT currently reachable through the app's own write path: the sole writer, lcWriteKnown() at account-v2.jsx:307, is always called with `.trim()`-ed values (`(form.first || '').trim()`), and grep confirms it is the only setItem site for LC_KNOWN_FIRST_KEY across source + compiled bundles. Only reachable via direct localStorage tampering (devtools/extension) today — same 'defensive gap, not a live bug' status the GStack team already assigned to the lc:auth-changed listener-atomicity finding. Recorded for parity/consistency, not blocking.

findings.evidence: Independent keyboard-only pass (Playwright Tab-press trace) on state (c): on modal open, document.activeElement is `button.lc-modal-close` (aria-label='Fermer'), NOT `#acc-email-connu`. One further Tab press reaches the email input. This corrects the audit brief's working assumption ('confirm focus genuinely lands on the email input first') — it does not, focus lands on the close button first. This is the generic WebModal component's documented behavior (components.jsx:339-352, `node.querySelector(focusable selector)` picks the first focusable DOM descendant, and the close button is rendered before {children}) — a standard WAI-ARIA APG-compliant pattern (focus moves into the dialog on open), not a defect. 'Ce n'est pas moi' IS reachable via keyboard (5 Tab presses from modal-open) and DOES activate via Enter (account-v2.jsx:513, onKeyDown handles both Enter and Space) — verified: after pressing Enter on it, both lecayenne.authPhone and lc_known_first read back null.
findings.fix_hint: No fix required — behavior is correct and standard. Flag only because neither account-trois-etats-2026-08-13.spec.js nor account-retour-connu-2026-08-13.spec.js contains any focus-order assertion at all (grep for 'focus'/'activeElement' in the latter returns zero hits) — this is a coverage gap worth closing in a future pass, not a defect today.

findings.evidence: account-v2.jsx lcKnownFresh(): `isFinite(at) && (Date.now() - at) <= LC_KNOWN_TTL_MS` — confirmed via direct source read that the 90-day boundary is INCLUSIVE (<=). The spec's two TTL cases seed at TTL_MS-1000 ('valid') and TTL_MS+1000 ('expired'). Neither lands ON the literal boundary (diff === TTL_MS exactly). Because both offsets sit strictly inside/outside the boundary, the test cannot actually distinguish `<=` from `<`: if a future edit silently tightened the comparison to strict `<`, both existing assertions would still pass unchanged (TTL_MS-1000 < TTL_MS either way; TTL_MS+1000 > TTL_MS either way). So the report's framing ('TTL boundary correct, ±1s around 90 days') is true of the current code (verified independently by reading the operator directly, not just by re-running the same class of offset test) but the spec itself does not operationally prove which operator is in effect at the exact edge.
findings.fix_hint: Add a 3rd TTL case seeding lc_known_first_at at exactly `Date.now() - TTL_MS` (diff === TTL_MS) and assert state (c) still shows (per current inclusive `<=`). That is the only offset that actually pins the operator. Not blocking — current behavior is correct by direct code inspection, this is a test-rigor gap, not a live bug.

lc_auth_changed_3rd_emitter_hunt.method: grep -rn "dispatchEvent.*lc:auth-changed" and "addEventListener.*lc:auth-changed" and a broader grep -rl "lc:auth-changed" across the ENTIRE repo (source + compiled/ + tools/seo/precompilation/compiled/), not limited to api.js/account-v2.jsx as the brief warned GStack might have missed a bundle or inline script.
lc_auth_changed_3rd_emitter_hunt.result: CONFIRMED — exactly ONE emitter site exists: api.js:170 inside setToken(). Exactly TWO addEventListener sites in source (racine.jsx:519, account-v2.jsx:194), each duplicated once in a compiled twin (compiled/racine.js:864, compiled/account-v2.js:337, plus tools/seo/precompilation/compiled/_racine.js:860 / _racine.jsx:516 — same racine.jsx listener, triplicated by the SEO precompilation pipeline, not a distinct 3rd independent listener). No service worker, no inline <script> in index.html references the event at all. Read both setToken(null) call sites directly (api.js:249 inside the 401 handler, api.js:343 inside logout()): both are immediately followed by `setPhone(null)` on the SAME statement. GStack's '0 orphan call sites, architecture fragility not a live bug' verdict is VERIFIED TRUE, not just re-asserted.

ttl_off_by_one.method: Read lcKnownFresh() operator directly (account-v2.jsx) instead of only re-running variants of the same ±1s test class.
ttl_off_by_one.result: Boundary is INCLUSIVE (<=) by direct source inspection — 90 days exactly is still 'known'. No off-by-one bug found. See finding C-003 for the test-rigor caveat (the spec's own ±1s cases don't actually prove which operator is active).
